seo.title: Program curriculum | APEX RN Prep
seo.description: The full APEX RN Prep curriculum: 11 weeks of live and self-study time, week-by-week topics, systems breakdown, sample teaching resources, and how practice and feedback work.

hero.title: Everything inside the 12 weeks.
hero.intro: Read the whole curriculum before you decide. Every week, every system, every question set and every mock exam is laid out below, so you can judge the plan for yourself.
hero.note: This page is for students who want the detail before they pay. Nothing here is a summary of a longer document.

structure.title: Live teaching, self-study, and homework that has a point.
structure.copy: Each week follows the same rhythm. Live sessions teach and coach in real time, self-study fills the gaps on your own schedule, and homework turns the topic into something you can recall under pressure.

items.title: Live sessions
items.copy: Two live online sessions a week, each about three hours, in a morning or evening batch. Replays are posted the same evening, so a missed class is never a lost week.
points: Concept teaching with slides, diagrams and flowcharts
Live practice with feedback in the moment
Questions asked and answered as they come up
Recording posted within hours of the session

items.title: Self-study between sessions
items.copy: A weekly reading pack and a self-study question set that match the live teaching, so nothing you read contradicts what you saw in class.
points: Weekly reading pack and study guide
60 self-study questions, untimed
One-page cheat sheet for the system of the week
Flashcard deck and vocabulary drill

items.title: Homework and follow-up
items.copy: Homework is short, specific and checked. It exists to find the gap while there is still time to fix it, not to fill an evening.
points: 40-80 timed questions, submitted before the next live session
Rationale review, not just a score
Weak topics are reworked the following week
A short written task most weeks: a care plan, a teaching sheet or a study plan

weeksIntro.title: Twelve weeks, in order.
weeksIntro.copy: This is the sequence we teach in. Weeks build on each other, so a missed week is repaired the following week rather than skipped.

weeks.title: Fundamentals & safety
weeks.summary: The base everything else stands on: safety, assessment, delegation, documentation, infection control and the nursing process used as a habit.
weeks.selfStudy: Reading pack, 60 self-study questions, safety cheat sheet
weeks.homework: 60 timed questions plus one nursing-process care plan
topics: Safety, error prevention and patient identifiers
Delegation, supervision and scope of practice
The nursing process applied to every scenario

weeks.title: MedSurg core systems I
weeks.summary: Cardiac, respiratory and renal: the load-bearing systems, the labs that move with them, and the priority problems that repeat on the exam.

weeks.homework: 80 timed questions plus one care plan for an unstable patient

weeks.title: MedSurg core systems II

GI bleeding, obstruction, pancreatitis and liver failure

weeks.title: MedSurg core systems III

weeks.title: Pharmacology

weeks.title: Maternity & OB

systems.title: Seven systems, mapped across the 11 weeks.
systems.copy: The program is built around the NCLEX-RN blueprint rather than a chapter list. This is where the teaching hours actually sit, and how each block is assessed.

items.title: Fundamentals & safety
items.description: Assessment, delegation, documentation, infection control and the nursing process, taught as the default you apply to every later system.
points: 6 live hours, 1 cheat sheet, 60 self-study questions
60 timed homework questions plus a care plan
Assessed by consolidation set and full mock exams

items.title: MedSurg core systems
items.description: The largest block: cardiac, respiratory, renal, neurologic, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, integumentary, endocrine, hematologic, immune and perioperative care, closing with shock, sepsis and multimorbidity.
points: 24 live hours across 4 weeks, 4 cheat sheets
240 self-study questions, 320 timed homework questions
One 100-question block consolidation set in week 5

items.title: Pharmacology
items.description: High-alert medications, therapeutic classes, adverse effects and the patient-safety checks that decide the answer when two options look right.
points: 6 live hours, 1 drug-class cheat sheet
60 self-study and 100 timed homework questions
Medication-administration task in the homework set

items.title: Maternity & OB
items.description: Antepartum through newborn care, including the monitoring, interventions and teaching that are tested in the maternal-newborn client.
points: 6 live hours, 1 maternal and newborn cheat sheet
60 self-study and 80 timed homework questions
Discharge-teaching task in the homework set

items.title: Pediatrics
items.description: Age bands, normal versus abnormal pediatric values, dosing, and family-centred care, with the normal ranges you are expected to know cold.
points: 6 live hours, 1 pediatric vital-signs cheat sheet
60 self-study and 80 timed homework questions
Age-band teaching plan in the homework set

items.title: Mental health & psych
items.description: Mental status assessment, therapeutic communication, legal and ethical boundaries, crisis care and psychiatric medications.
points: 6 live hours, 1 mental-health nursing cheat sheet
60 self-study and 80 timed homework questions
Care plan task for a patient in crisis

items.title: NGN practice sessions
items.description: Extended sessions in the Next Generation NCLEX format, then two full-length mocks, so the reasoning is practised under the same pressure as test day.
points: 12 live hours, 1 NGN reasoning cheat sheet
6 NGN cases, 60 self-study and 60 timed questions
2 full-length mock exams with written review

practice.title: Questions, mocks, and a plan for what you keep missing.
practice.copy: Practice is scheduled, not optional. The quantity is set, the feedback is written, and the weak areas you keep missing are reworked the following week.

NGN cases worked step by step in week 10
full-length mock exams under timed conditions

steps.title: Set weekly volume
steps.copy: Every week carries a fixed number of questions: 60 self-study, untimed, then 40-80 homework, timed. By week five you are working 100-120 in a sitting, which is exam pace.

steps.title: Every question gets a rationale
steps.copy: Homework is returned with the reasoning for each item, including the option you chose and why it was not the safest answer. A score on its own does not teach.

steps.title: Weak areas are reworked
steps.copy: Question sets are tagged by system. When the same tag comes back below target, it is rebuilt into the following week as targeted practice and called out in the live session.

steps.title: Reviewed live, then written down
steps.copy: The live session opens with the previous week's misses. You leave each week with a short written weak-area plan: what to review, what question types to drill, and by when.

steps.title: Mock exams close the loop
steps.copy: The two full-length mocks in week 11 are reviewed the same way, then turned into the final-week study plan you take into test day.

finalCta.title: Read the plan, then talk to a person.
finalCta.copy: If something here does not fit your timeline or your exam date, say so. We will tell you honestly whether the program is right for you or whether you need a shorter plan.
